why: Build review M1: rule T2's text checks could be bypassed in Lean. A def named with an escaped identifier containing a block-comment opener (def «/-» ... def «-/») hides the code between from tests_m3/_i42.py::lean_code and from holon.lean.strip_comments (so from check_text's forbidden scan too), e.g. a macro_rules that rewrites `=`; Lean then accepts weakened theorems whose text still equals the frozen statements (the reviewer's demo checked, with cor_6_5_potentials elaborated to True). The check now also refuses any escaped identifier after the marker and applies holon.lean.FORBIDDEN to this contract's own comment-free reading. Stricter only: the committed Theory.lean has no escaped identifier and passes; a new test (test_lean_elaborated_types_are_the_frozen_ones, not preregistered) compares each frozen theorem's elaborated type under pp.all. holon.lean.strip_comments itself is in the holon-ir/0.2 and 0.3 generator closures, so it is reported for the lead, not changed here.

Build review M2: rule T7's text checks could be bypassed in Bend. They strip `#...` comments line by line without regard to string literals, so a record pattern after a "#" string in a one-line match was invisible, and a helper opening the record proved per-edge facts by computation while dead `_a = avail_0(h)` lines satisfied the naming check (the reviewer's demo passed bend, --verdict and this test). The check now refuses string and char literals in an instance PROOF.bend (so `#` always starts a comment) and requires each bridge_* body to be exactly `match h:`, one record case, `{==}`. Stricter only: the committed proofs have no literal and their bridges have that form.

Build review M2 (the same hole as rule T7's): the canary PROOF.bend's record checks read lines with `#...` removed regardless of strings; the check now refuses string and char literals there too, so `#` always starts a comment. Stricter only: the committed canary proofs have none.
